newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits fall 5.0 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits fall 5.0 pct in February.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in March fell 5.0 percent to C$2.43 billion, seasonally adjusted, from February, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Mar Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 1.2 percent after a 4.7 percent rise in February.

For the quarter, building permits issued in the first quarter rose 12.4 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996 to C$7.42 billion, Statistics Canada said. Residential permits rose 13.5 percent to C$4.7 billion and non-residential permits rose 10.4 percent to C$2.7 billion.

Statistics Canada said the housing sector maintained its momentum in the first quarter of 1997, assisted by favorable prices and low mortgage rates. The federal agency did not give reasons for the five percent drop on the month.
The agency said the value of residential building permits rose for the third straight quarter to the highest level since the first quarter of 1990.
StatsCan said the 13.5 percent rise in residential permits in the quarter was due mainly to an increase in the value of permits for single family dwellings.

The agency said renewed consumer confidence and more affordable housing make the short-term outlook for new housing construction positive, especially if mortgage rates and housing prices remain relatively stable.
Quarterly gains in non-residential construction intentions were partly offset by a decline in commercial construction permits, StatsCan said.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contstruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
